name: locksettle
description: Fix lockfile merge conflicts the right way. Detects conflict markers in package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, go.sum, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock and Pipfile.lock, checks the manifest first, then regenerates the lockfile with the right tool in a visible task.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace LockSettle only reads lockfiles and manifests to show conflict warnings. It runs no git command and no package manager until the workspace is trusted.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No lockfile has merge conflict markers.
LockSettle watches package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, go.sum, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock and Pipfile.lock for merge conflicts, and regenerates a conflicted one with its own package manager after the manifest is resolved.
[Rescan lockfiles](command:locksettle.rescan)

No lockfile has merge conflict markers.
LockSettle watches package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, go.sum, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock and Pipfile.lock for merge conflicts. In this untrusted workspace it only shows warnings; git and package managers run after you trust the folder.
[Rescan lockfiles](command:locksettle.rescan)
[Manage Workspace Trust](command:workbench.trust.manage)

lockfile.description: Workspace-relative path of the lockfile to regenerate.

locksettle.enabled.description: Watch the workspace for lockfiles with merge conflict markers.

locksettle.notify.description: Show one notification when a lockfile gets merge conflict markers.

locksettle.codeLens.description: Show a Regenerate CodeLens on line 1 of a conflicted lockfile.

locksettle.lockfileBase.markdownDescription: Starting point for the lockfile before the tool runs, per ecosystem. `keep` leaves the conflict markers in (default for npm, yarn and pnpm, which merge both sides themselves), `ours` runs `git checkout --ours -- <lockfile>` (default for all others), `theirs` runs `git checkout --theirs`. During a rebase git swaps the meaning of ours and theirs. Example: `{"npm": "ours"}`.

locksettle.yarnFlavor.markdownDescription: Yarn version. `auto` reads the `packageManager` field of package.json, then looks for `.yarnrc.yml`, then at the lockfile format.

locksettle.poetryVersion.markdownDescription: Poetry major version. `auto` reads the `@generated by Poetry X` header of poetry.lock (Poetry 2 when unknown). Poetry 1 uses `poetry lock --no-update`, Poetry 2 uses `poetry lock`.

locksettle.commands.npm.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for npm. Empty uses the built-in `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.yarn.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for yarn. Empty uses the built-in `yarn install --ignore-scripts (classic) / yarn install --mode=update-lockfile (berry)`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is. Also applies to Yarn berry unless `locksettle.commands.yarnBerry` is set.

locksettle.commands.yarnBerry.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for yarnBerry. Empty uses the built-in `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.pnpm.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for pnpm. Empty uses the built-in `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.poetry.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for poetry. Empty uses the built-in `poetry lock --no-update (Poetry 1) / poetry lock (Poetry 2)`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.uv.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for uv. Empty uses the built-in `uv lock`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.cargo.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for cargo. Empty uses the built-in `cargo update --workspace`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.go.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for go. Empty uses the built-in `go mod tidy`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.composer.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for composer. Empty uses the built-in `composer update --lock --no-install --no-scripts`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.bundler.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for bundler. Empty uses the built-in `bundle lock`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.

locksettle.commands.pipenv.markdownDescription: Command that regenerates the lockfile for pipenv. Empty uses the built-in `pipenv lock`. A string is split into words without a shell (quotes are supported); an array is used as is.
